name: stage3-machinery-walls-v1
title: Stage 3 machinery walls and walkways (2/1 world pages)
state: predicted-static; import only after live capture confirms the key (validate_predicted.py confirm + gate on the AQ-03 Stage 3 capture)
method:
W7-STAGE3 index masters (copy of w7-stage2/tools/s2master.py; imports s3lib): one CLUT-free master per 4bpp page, rendered through any CLUT.

Master (8 px/texel = the 2048 export grid; CPU only, deterministic, no AI, nothing added):
  categorical layer  top-3 (label, weight u8) per pixel: for every native index i the one-hot mask is upsampled
                     texel-centred (bilinear), gaussian-smoothed (sigma_cat texels) and raised to power_cat, then
                     normalised (w7-stage7 build_s7 / w4-world catsoft method). It carries the class (alpha) of ANY
                     CLUT: class = class of the strongest visible label where visible weight >= 0.5, else 0, so every
                     CLUT gets its own native class map with smooth contours.
  continuous layer   t (float16, NaN elsewhere) inside regions whose drawn CLUTs are monotone luminance ramps over the
                     indices used there (palette-cycling lights, smoke and flame ramps): normalised convolution of the
                     native index over the texels that are visible in that region (bilinear texel-centred upsample,
                     gaussian sigma_t texels); render = lerp(P[floor t], P[ceil t]) (index_pipeline convention), t
                     clamped to the CLUT's visible run.
Render(CLUT) -> RGBA at 8 px/texel; the native class is then forced at every native texel centre floor((i+0.5)*s)
(one pixel each, w6/w7 rule) and every export is re-read and validated (0 mismatches required).
Regions come from the Stage 2 draw records (work/draws-s2.json): every drawn uv rect of every key of the page whose CLUT
words are known (static export CLUT or CRC-validated recovered phase).
builder_doc:
W7-STAGE3 builder: first Stage 3 art families on exact-static, single-writer pages of the frozen stages-v4 export.

    python -I build_s3.py <family> [freeze]      family = walls | signage
    -> staging/<name>/ (default) or frozen/<name>/ (freeze: immutable, refuses to overwrite)

State of every key: predicted-static; import only after live capture confirms the key (validate_predicted.py confirm +
gate on the AQ-03 Stage 3 capture).  No Stage 3 capture exists, so there are no draw records and no runtime CLUT phases:
  * pages: exact-static TEX with a single writer (2/1, the main member that carries the stage CLUT block); words from
    stages-v4/stage3/textures (crc32 == TEX and sha256 == FREEZE.json re-checked);
  * keys: listed predictions of those pages whose CLUT is a static stage-owned CLUT (owner 2/1 = stage CLUT block, or
    2/0 = 16x1 records of the stage overlay), not all-transparent, with the highest coverage = pair_count (how often the
    CLUT/page pair occurs in the stage model data) >= MIN_PAIRS and visible texels >= MIN_VIS of the page.  The all-zero
    CLUT 190A55AD keys that the export labels exact-static are transparent and are not exported;
  * cells: inferred from page content (s3cells.py, calibrated on Stage 2 draw rects, work/cells-calibration.json) and
    rendered in isolation, the Stage 2 v2 rule; replaced by real UV rects once AQ-03 exists.
Method (Stage 2 method, w7-stage2 s2master copied as s3master): CLUT-free categorical index master at 8 px/texel
(sigma 0.30 texel, power 4.0: exact native colours on plateaus, smooth contours), class forced and validated at every
native texel centre.  CPU only, deterministic; no generated imagery; nothing invented (no new text, colours or pixels).
cells_doc:
Static cell inference for atlas pages without draw records (Stage 3 has no capture yet).

Stage 2 draw records showed world atlas cells are rectangles on the 32-texel grid (plus small sprites).  Without UVs, a
32x32 block grid is joined into cells: two neighbouring blocks belong to one cell unless the 32-texel segment between
them is a content seam, i.e. the mean absolute index jump ACROSS the line is clearly larger than the jumps on the two
column (row) pairs next to it on either side:  across > ratio * max(within_a, within_b) and across > min_jump.
A continuous texture (a tiling wall, one big panel) has no seam inside, so it stays one cell; a change of texture at a
grid line separates the cells.  Cells are connected components of blocks (any shape); render isolation uses the
component mask (texels outside the component are filled with the nearest component texel before rendering, and only
the component's own pixels are pasted).  This is an inference: it is replaced by real UV rects after the AQ-03 capture.

class_validation.rule: class at every native texel centre floor((i+0.5)*scale) == classes(CLUT)[words] (0 = 0x0000, 255 = STP, 127 = opaque); every export re-read from disk

known_limits: predicted keys only: no Stage 3 capture exists; PAL pairings are candidates from the model data (Stage 1 calibration: 160 of 3,052 likely page keys were observed), so some exported keys may never be drawn

cells are inferred from content on the 32-texel grid (calibration on Stage 2 draw rects at ratio 1.6: 12 of 208 interior lines falsely cut, 216 of 437 drawn-rect edges detected); small sprites inside a block are not isolated
categorical master: exact native colours and smooth contours, no generated material detail (CPU only; the GPU is down)
honest_read: Inspected staging review sheets 01-13 (2026-11-13, lane-s3). What it is: a contour-smoothed native, not a remastered surface. Colours are the exact native CLUT entries and the class map is exact (50 files, 0 mismatches), but there is no new material detail: every flat plateau is perfectly flat, so plates read as smooth plastic at 4K. At the 9 px/texel in-game SIMULATION it is clean and no longer blocky, and slightly softer than native. At 16x the weaknesses show: 1-texel lines (66A350AA vertical stripes, 59B55BC8 trim) bead and pinch, dithered stipple (66A350AA plate grime, B53A4C57 lower panels) becomes rounded blob mottling, and diagonal hazard stripes become rounded lozenges. Small native digits on 59B55BC8 ("1910"-like plate marks) keep their topology but get rounded corners. 8 of the 25 keys (B53A4C57 with 0584767D, 114545DB, 1E925EC8, 558EE0EC, 77620CF9, D9B206FA, F63AB6BA, FFF96EC9 at 7-11% visible) are 2-entry CLUTs: only two indices are visible, as scattered specks (near-black 8,8,8 for 1E925EC8/558EE0EC/D9B206FA, a dark-red pair for 114545DB, green/red/yellow/blue indicator pairs for the others). They are probably indicator-light or overlay passes, or wrong PAL pairings; harmless, but whether they are drawn is unknown. Whole-page renders under a non-owning CLUT (for example B53A4C57-A02A0ECB, all teal) only matter in the cells that CLUT really draws, which is unknown until AQ-03. Verdict: usable baseline that removes blockiness, not an HD surface; material layering is required before this can be called a remaster.
